title: Using Code Coverage to Assess Feature Gaps in MPI Correctness Tool Classification Tests
problem: MPI-BugBench (MBB), a code-generator-based MPI correctness testing framework, has incomplete coverage of MPI features (e.g., varying-count collectives) and limited code structure diversity in generated tests, reducing effectiveness of testing tools like MUST, PARCOACH, and clang-tidy.
motivation: Existing MPI correctness benchmarks rely on pruning test sets based on real-world usage patterns, but this approach misses edge cases and advanced features. Testing tool verification is incomplete, hindering detection of subtle correctness bugs.
method: Analyze code coverage triggered by MBB tests in three MPI correctness tools. Use coverage analysis to identify missing MPI features and code structures. Implement 34 new tests covering previously uncovered scenarios (varying-count collectives, loops, array-based handles).
key_novelty: First comprehensive code-coverage analysis of MPI correctness benchmarks; identifies and addresses missing feature coverage through targeted test generation.
contributions: Code coverage analysis of MPI-BugBench against MUST, PARCOACH, clang-tidy
Identification of feature gaps: varying-count collectives, limited code structure diversity
34 new test cases covering previously uncovered MPI features
Quantification of coverage improvements (e.g., single varying-count test adds 770 covered lines in MUST)

metrics.coverage_example: Single varying-count collectives test: 770 additional covered lines in MUST
metrics.focus: Completeness of feature coverage and tool analysis capability

limitations: Abstract only - no performance metrics, no analysis of false positive/negative rates in tools, limited detail on which MPI features are still missing
